findings.evidence: template/scripts/managed_project_status.py:427 reads Status, then lines 429–435 unconditionally write Backlog if that earlier read was unset. A writer assigning In progress between the read and mutation is overwritten; the final check at lines 437–442 sees Backlog and succeeds. An in-memory execution of the candidate function reproduced this outcome. This violates openspec/changes/requirement-project-membership/specs/managed-task-intake/spec.md:5: 'an existing Status SHALL NOT be overwritten.'
findings.summary: Membership repair can overwrite a concurrently assigned Status and still report success.

findings.evidence: docs/engineering/chatgpt-project-protocol.md:83–89 says fixation succeeds after read-back verifies the labels and that a fixation-only request 'then stops', without checking Project membership. The candidate adds the membership gate only in the later sequence at lines 232–238, while template/docs/engineering/chatgpt-project-protocol.md:86–94 updates the adapter itself. The central adapter therefore retains the behavior prohibited by openspec/changes/requirement-project-membership/specs/managed-task-intake/spec.md:26, which requires confirmed membership before reporting fixation.
findings.summary: The central connected-authoring adapter still directs fixation to stop after label verification, leaving conflicting completion instructions.
